summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of failed kidney transplant presented with a pruritic rash affecting his hands, feet, and eyes, which began hours after receiving cefazolin during a thrombolytic procedure for a dialysis fistula clot. Evaluation revealed no signs of infection or fistula complications. The rash and symptoms were attributed to an allergic reaction to cefazolin, supported by his documented allergy and improvement with diphenhydramine and artificial tears. Blood tests confirmed eosinophilia, a long-standing finding previously evaluated and deemed of unknown origin. A chest X-ray showed stable, slowly progressive micronodular interstitial disease, likely hypersensitivity pneumonia, with no acute infection. The patient responded well to treatment, completed inpatient hemodialysis, and was discharged home with instructions to avoid cefazolin, use short-term antihistamines and eye drops, and follow up with his primary care provider regarding eosinophilia.
problems: Dermatitis due to drugs and medicines taken internally
